idiom_name: pimpl (pointer-to-implementation) class with out-of-line special members
implementation_notes: A C++ class is only as self-contained as its header: private data members and private non-virtual member functions are part of the definition every user compiles against, and any change to them recompiles all users, so naming a neighbouring model type there forces every reader and every rebuild to depend on it. The classic realization is therefore the pimpl idiom - declare `class impl;` and hold `std::unique_ptr<impl>` - with the impl class and all private logic in the .cpp and the special members declared in the header and defined out-of-line where the impl type is complete. Access control plus namespaces keep helpers private, and non-member functions in the same namespace keep the interface minimal. Since C++20 a module interface with a private module fragment achieves the same isolation with no indirection; the hand-written pimpl remains right for ABI-stable library headers and pre-C++20 toolchains.
pitfalls: `std::unique_ptr` requires the impl type to be complete wherever the deleter is instantiated, so the destructor, move constructor and move assignment must be declared in the header and defined in the .cpp or the class fails to compile for its users.
Every call through the pimpl is an indirection plus, usually, one allocation: for small values that are copied often, a plain value type with everything in the header is faster and simpler.
A raw pointer member breaks const propagation - use `std::experimental::propagate_const` or provide both const and non-const forwarding overloads.
A pimpl class can never be header-only, and without link-time optimisation the inline performance of small member functions is lost.

variants.name: C++20 module interface with a private module fragment
variants.idiom_name: export module + module : private; (or a non-exported implementation unit)
variants.implementation_notes: With C++20 the boundary moves from the class to the translation unit: export the class from the module interface unit and keep private helpers either in a separate, non-exported implementation unit or behind `module : private;`, where definitions are not reachable from importers at all. No pointer, no allocation and no out-of-line special members are needed, const-correctness works normally, and recompilation is contained at the module boundary - the strongest form of the pattern the language offers. Prefer it when the toolchain is C++20 and modules are the primary build interface; keep the pimpl form for older standards and for headers published with an ABI promise.
pitfalls: A private module fragment may appear only in the primary module interface unit, which then must be the module's only unit - it cannot be combined with module partitions, so larger modules need a non-exported implementation unit instead.
Everything declared before `module : private;` is still part of the interface, so the isolation covers only what comes after the marker; put the marker before the first private helper.
Module support is still uneven across compilers and build systems; falling back to headers silently reintroduces the compilation dependencies the variant was chosen to remove.
